rules.rule_text: This Chapter does not include waxes of heading/subheading 27.12 or 34.04. rules.rule_text: In heading/subheading 27.10 - 'Fuel oil' - fuel composed entirely or mainly of refining residues, which in a viscosity test according to ASTM D 445 method will have a viscosity at 50 degrees Celsius higher than 50 centistokes; 'Low sulfur fuel oil' - such fuel oil, whose sulfur content according to test method ASTM D4294 does not exceed 0.50% by weight.

In heading/subheading 27.10 - 'Diesel oil' - a liquid hydrocarbon distillate permitted for use by law or that meets all of the following: Density less than 870 kg/m³ according to ASTM D 1298 test, and at least 70% by volume evaporates between 200°C and 400°C according to distillation test by ASTM D 86 method.

This Chapter does not include: 1. Organic compounds with a separate chemical definition, except for pure methane and propane classified in subheading 27.11; [References: subheading 27.11 – Petroleum gases and other gaseous hydrocarbons.]

In heading/subheading 27.10 - 'Petrol' (BENZINE) – a liquid hydrocarbon distillate permitted for use in a motor vehicle by law or that in a distillation test by ASTM D 86 method, at least 75% of its volume evaporates within the range of 30 to 200 degrees Celsius.

This Chapter does not include: Sludges from storage tanks of petroleum oils, consisting mainly of these oils (heading/subheading 27.10); [References: heading 27.10 – Petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals, other than crude; preparations not elsewhere specified or included, containing by weight 70 % or more of petroleum oils or of oils obtained...]

For the purposes of heading/subheading 38.25 the expression 'other waste' refers to other waste from the chemical industry or from allied industries. The expression 'other waste' in any case does not include waste that contains mainly petroleum oils or oils obtained from bituminous minerals (heading/subheading 27.10). [References: heading 27.10 – Petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals, other than crude; preparations not elsewhere specified or included, containing by weight 70

This Chapter does not include preparations for sticking which are in heading/subheading 27.10 or 34.03. [References: heading 27.10 – Petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals, other than crude; preparations not elsewhere specified or included, containing by weight 70 % or more of petroleum oils or of oils obtained...; subheading 34.03 – Lubricating preparations (including cuttingoil preparations, bolt or nut release preparations, antirust or anticorrosion preparations and mould r

In heading/subheading 34.03, the expression "petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals" relates to the products defined in Note 2 to Chapter 27. [References: chapter 27 – Mineral fuels, mineral oils and products of their distillation; bituminous substances; mineral waxes]

For the purposes of heading/subheading 27.10, the term 'waste oils' refers to waste containing mainly petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals (as described in Note 2 to this Chapter), whether or not mixed with water; including sludge oils from storage tanks of petroleum oils, mainly containing these oils and a high concentration of additives (such as chemicals) used in the production of primary products.

For the purposes of heading/subheading 27.10, the term 'waste oils' refers to waste containing mainly petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals (as described in Note 2 to this Chapter), whether or not mixed with water; including these oils in the form of emulsions in water or mixtures thereof with water such as those resulting from oil spills, washing storage tanks or from use in cutting oils for mechanical processing operations.

This Chapter does not include: Vegetable fats and oils (Chapter 15); [References: chapter 15 – Animal, vegetable or microbial fats and oils and their cleavage products; prepared edible fats; animal or vegetable waxes]

The heading/subheading does not apply to products in headings/subheadings 15.16, 34.02, or 38.23 even if they have a waxy characteristic. [References: heading 15.16 – Animal, vegetable or microbial fats and oils and their fractions, partly or wholly hydrogenated, interesterified, reesterified or elaidinised, whether or not refined, but not further prepared.; heading 34.02 – Organic surfaceactive agents (other than soap); surfaceactive preparations, washing preparations (including auxiliary washi

Heading/subheading 15.18 does not include fats or oils or their fractions, merely deodorized, which are classified in the heading/subheading covering fats and oils and their fractions, not deodorized.

Subject to the instructions of Rule 1 of Part VI, this Chapter does not include: Metals, whether or not pure, metal alloys, or cermets including sintered metal carbides (metal carbides sintered with metal) in Chapter XV. [References: chapter 15 – Animal, vegetable or microbial fats and oils and their cleavage products; prepared edible fats; animal or vegetable waxes]

For the purposes of heading/subheading 27.10, the term 'waste oils' refers to waste containing mainly petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals (as described in Note 2 to this Chapter), whether or not mixed with water; including oils no longer suitable for use as primary products, for example used lubricating oils, used hydraulic oils and used transformer oils.

Subject to the instructions of Rule 1 of Part VI, this Chapter does not include: Metals, whether or not pure, metal alloys, or cermets including sintered metal carbides (metal carbides sintered with metal) in Chapter XV. [References: chapter 15 – Animal, vegetable or microbial fats and oils and their cleavage products; prepared edible fats; animal or vegetable waxes]

68.06, 70.19 - Mineral wool for thermal insulation
This guideline is intended to clarify the meaning of the term "mineral wool used for thermal insulation" appearing in the Second Annex to the Free Import Order.
This mineral wool comes in the form of fibers and is produced by melting rocks, slag, glass, or a mixture of all these.

guidelines.title: 61.15 Hosiery
guidelines.text: A sock containing rubber threads only in its upper part intended to secure the sock to the leg shall not be considered graduated compression hosiery within the meaning of subheading 61.15.1000. Classification Ruling: 61.15 029/88.

Clothing in this Section designed to close left over right in front shall be regarded as men's or boys' clothing, and those designed to close right over left in front as women's or girls' clothing. These provisions shall not apply where the cut of the garment clearly indicates that it is designed for one or other of the sexes. [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; subheading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

guidelines.text:
68.06, 70.19 - Mineral wool for thermal insulation
This guideline is intended to clarify the meaning of the term "mineral wool used for thermal insulation" appearing in the Second Annex to the Free Import Order.
This mineral wool comes in the form of fibers and is produced by melting rocks, slag, glass, or a mixture of all these.
Mineral wool imported in bulk, in shaped sheets, or in rolls is classified under heading 68.06 or heading 70.19, as applicable, and is subject to Standard SI 751. 002/9

guidelines.title: Food preparations
guidelines.text: Food preparations: Since casein is the primary natural protein found in milk, it is not possible to detect via laboratory testing the addition of 3% of the protein substitute known as "sodium caseinate" to goods classified in Chapter 4, such as dried milk or milk-based powders. The small addition of the protein substitute does not significantly affect the properties of the goods. (Therefore, classification instruction No. 15/97 from 1997 "Food Preparation" for heading 19.01 is canceled as of 01.

guidelines.text: 34.01, 34.02 - Preparations for washing the hands or the body, which are not suitable for classification under heading 34.01, shall be classified under heading 34.02. rules.rule_text: This Chapter does not include waxes of heading/subheading 27.12 or 34.04. [References: heading 27.12 – Petroleum jelly; paraffin wax, microcrystalline petroleum wax, slack wax, ozokerite, lignite wax, peat wax, other mineral waxes, and similar products obtained by synthesis or by other processes,...; subheading 34.04 – Artificial waxes and prepared waxes.]

In heading/subheading 34.04, subject to the exceptions provided for below, the expression 'artificial waxes and prepared waxes' relates only to those: Organic products produced by a chemical process, having a waxy character, whether or not soluble in water;

In heading/subheading 34.04, subject to the exceptions provided for below, the expression 'artificial waxes and prepared waxes' relates only to those: Products having a waxy character, based on one or more waxes and containing fats, resins, mineral substances or other substances.

This Chapter does not include: Enzymatic preparations for steeping or retting or other products in Chapter 34; [References: chapter 34 – Soap, organic surfaceactive agents, washing preparations, lubricating preparations, artificial waxes, prepared waxes, polishing or scouring preparations, candles and similar articles, modelling...]

This Chapter does not include: Fatty acids, processed waxes, medicaments, dyes, varnishes, soap, preparations for perfumery, cosmetics or toiletries, sulphonated oils or other goods in Chapter VI; [References: section VI – Section VI: PRODUCTS OF THE CHEMICAL OR ALLIED INDUSTRIES]

The heading/subheading does not apply to mineral waxes or similar products of heading/subheading 27.12, whether or not mixed together or merely coloured. [References: heading 27.12 – Petroleum jelly; paraffin wax, microcrystalline petroleum wax, slack wax, ozokerite, lignite wax, peat wax, other mineral waxes, and similar products obtained by synthesis or by other processes,...]

In heading/subheading 27.10 - Waxy distillate - a liquid hydrocarbon distillate, the final boiling point of which exceeds 370 degrees Celsius, and not more than thirty percent by volume distills at a temperature of 357 degrees Celsius.

Subject to the instructions of Rule 1 of Part VI, this Chapter does not include: Metals, whether or not pure, metal alloys, or cermets including sintered metal carbides (metal carbides sintered with metal) in Chapter XV. [References: chapter 15 – Animal, vegetable or microbial fats and oils and their cleavage products; prepared edible fats; animal or vegetable waxes]

The heading/subheading does not apply to unmixed waxes of animal or unmixed waxes of vegetable origin, whether or not refined or coloured, in heading/subheading 15.21. [References: heading 15.21 – Vegetable waxes (other than triglycerides), beeswax, other insect waxes and spermaceti, whether or not refined or coloured.]

rules.rule_text: This Chapter does not include: Preparations of headings/subheadings 33.03 to 33.07, even if they have therapeutic or prophylactic properties. [References: heading 33.03 – Perfumes and toilet waters.; heading 33.04 – Beauty or makeup preparations and preparations for the care of the skin (other than medicaments), including sunscreen or sun tan preparations; manicure or pedicure preparations.; heading 33.05 – Preparations for use on the hair.; heading 33.06 – Preparations for oral or dental hygien

The subheading 13.02 does not refer to extracts for tanning or dyeing (heading/subheading 32.01 or 32.03); [References: heading 32.01 – Tanning extracts of vegetable origin; tannins and their salts, ethers, esters and other derivatives.; subheading 32.03 – Colouring matter of vegetable or animal origin (including dyeing extracts but excluding animal black), whether or not chemically defined; preparations as specified in Note 3 to this Chapter based on...]

This Chapter does not include items in Chapter 32 (such as brightening agents); [References: chapter 32 – Tanning or dyeing extracts; tannins and their derivatives; dyes, pigments and other colouring matter; paints and varnishes; putty and other mastics; inks]

This Chapter does not include shampoos, dentifrices, shaving creams and foams or bath preparations, containing soap or other organic surface-active agents (headings/subheadings 33.05, 33.06 or 33.07). [References: heading 33.05 – Preparations for use on the hair.; heading 33.06 – Preparations for oral or dental hygiene, including denture fixative pastes and powders; yarn used to clean between the teeth (dental floss), in individual retail packages.; heading 33.07 – Preshave, shaving or aftershav

guidelines.title: 33.05 Developer cream containing hydrogen peroxide
guidelines.text: 33.05 Developer cream containing hydrogen peroxide Developer cream containing hydrogen peroxide and additional chemical substances (such as: surfactants, disinfectants, oils, acids, etc., common in the cosmetics or soap industries) and which is manufactured for the purpose of use as an auxiliary preparation for hair treatment, whether as an additive to hair dye (developer) or as a preparation for lightening the color. Its classification is in subheading 33.05.9000. File SHM-33.05 005/94

guidelines.title: 34.02 Preparations for washing the hands or the body.
guidelines.text: 34.01, 34.02 - Preparations for washing the hands or the body, which are not suitable for classification under heading 34.01, shall be classified under heading 34.02. The term "preparations for washing" means liquid preparations whose solid and/or molded counterparts are classified under heading 34.01. Therefore, this term does not include shampoo, bath foam, perfumed bath salts, and similar preparations. File 033/93 1091/72

guidelines.title: 87.05 Sweeper vehicles
guidelines.text: Those meeting the basic definition of a vehicle, as explained in the Explanatory Notes to the Brussels Nomenclature, are classified under heading 87.05 of the Customs Tariff as motor vehicles for special purposes. These vehicles can be of various sizes, ranging from large municipal vehicles to small vehicles for cleaning small and confined areas such as warehouses, docks, etc. File SHM: 87.05 018/93

guidelines.text: Cassette holders for motor vehicles and decorative strips cut to size for motor vehicles shall be classified under customs subheading 87.08.9990. Classification Case: 87.08 010/97.

rules.rule_text: This Chapter does not include: Preparations of headings/subheadings 33.03 to 33.07, even if they have therapeutic or prophylactic properties. [References: heading 33.03 – Perfumes and toilet waters.; heading 33.04 – Beauty or makeup preparations and preparations for the care of the skin (other than medicaments), including sunscreen or sun tan preparations; manicure or pedicure preparations.; heading 33.05 – Preparations for use on the hair.; heading 33.06 – Preparations for oral or dental hygien
This Chapter does not include: Perfumery or toilet preparations (Chapter 33).

This Chapter does not include: Wadding, felt or nonwovens, impregnated, coated or covered with substances or preparations (such as perfumery or cosmetics of Chapter 33, soaps or detergents of heading/subheading 34.01, polishing preparations, creams and similar preparations of heading/subheading 34.05, fabric-softeners of heading/subheading 38.09) where the textile material is present purely in a carrier role. [References: chapter 33 – Essential oils and resinoids; perfumery, cosmetic or toilet p
This Chapter does not include: Perfumery, cosmetic or toilet preparations (Chapter 33). [References: chapter 33 – Essential oils and resinoids; perfumery, cosmetic or toilet preparations]

This Chapter does not include: Fatty acids, processed waxes, medicaments, dyes, varnishes, soap, preparations for perfumery, cosmetics or toiletries, sulphonated oils or other goods in Chapter VI; [References: section VI – Section VI: PRODUCTS OF THE CHEMICAL OR ALLIED INDUSTRIES]

Subheading 12.11 refers, inter alia, to the following plants or parts thereof: Basil, Hyssop, Ginseng, Origanum, Lily, all types of Mint, Rosemary, Rue, Sage and Wormwood. However, subheading 12.11 does not refer to these goods: preparations for perfumery, cosmetic or toilet use in Chapter 33. [References: chapter 33 – Essential oils and resinoids; perfumery, cosmetic or toilet preparations]

This Chapter does not include: Perfumed papers or papers impregnated or coated with cosmetics (Chapter 33); [References: chapter 33 – Essential oils and resinoids; perfumery, cosmetic or toilet preparations]

guidelines.text: Under this heading, structures shall be classified, whether assembled or unassembled, provided that the structural components are imported complete and ready for assembly. Goods for the completion of a structure - such as: wall-to-wall floor carpets, curtains, when cut to sizes suitable for defined parts of the structure, roof tiles and floor tiles in the required quantity - shall be classified with the structure, provided they are imported together with it. rules.rule_text: This Chapter does not include furniture which is a toy or lamps and lighting fittings which are toys (heading/subheading 95.03), billiard tables or other furniture specially constructed for games (heading/subheading 95.04), furniture for conjuring tricks or decorations (other than lighting chains), such as Chinese lanterns (heading/subheading 95.05). [References: heading 95.03 – Tricycles, scooters, pedal cars and similar wheeled toys; dolls carriages; dolls; other toys; reducedsize ("scale") mo

Heading/subheading 66.03 does not include parts, decorations or accessories of textile materials, or covers, sheaths, straps, umbrella sheaths and the like, of any material. Such goods, presented together, but not fitted to the articles of heading/subheading 66.01 or 66.02, are classified separately and are not considered as parts of those articles. [References: heading 66.01 – Umbrellas and sun umbrellas (including walkingstick umbrellas, garden umbrellas and similar umbrellas).; heading 66.02

Heading 39.25 refers only to architectural ornaments and decorations, such as flutings, cupolas, dovecotes; and also ornamental fountains, which are not products included in any preceding heading in Chapter Subheading II. [References: chapter 39 – Plastics and articles thereof]

In the entire Supplement, the expression 'parts for general use' means items in headings/subheadings 83.01, 83.02, 83.08, 83.10, and frames and mirrors of base metal, in heading/subheading 83.06. [References: heading 83.01 – Padlocks and locks (key, combination or electrically operated), of base metal; clasps and frames with clasps, incorporating locks, of base metal; keys for any of the foregoing articles, of base metal.; heading 83.02 – Base metal mountings, fittings and similar articles suita

For the purposes of heading/subheading 64.06, the term "parts" does not include nails (pegs), buckles, eyelet rings, hooks, fasteners, ornaments, braids, laces, pompons or other trimmings (to be classified in the appropriate headings/subheadings) or buttons or other goods of heading/subheading 96.06. [References: heading 96.06 – Buttons, pressfasteners, snapfasteners and pressstuds, button moulds and other parts of these articles; button blanks.]

The expressions 'parts' and 'parts and accessories' do not refer to items in heading/subheading 83.06, if they can be identified as being for goods in this part or not. [References: heading 83.06 – Bells, gongs and the like, nonelectric, of base metal; statuettes and other ornaments, of base metal; photograph, picture or similar frames, of base metal; mirrors of base metal.]

Headings/Subheadings 44.14 to 44.21 refer to the items described therein, made of particle board or similar board, fiberboard, laminated wood or densified wood, as they refer to such items made of wood. [References: heading 44.14 – Wooden frames for paintings, photographs, mirrors or similar objects.; heading 44.15 – Packing cases, boxes, crates, drums and similar packings, of wood; cabledrums of wood; pallets, box pallets and other load boards, of wood; pallet collars of wood.; heading 44.16 –

For the purposes of heading/subheading 71.14, the expression "articles of goldsmiths' or silversmiths' wares" includes items such as ornaments, tableware, toilet articles, smoking accessories, and other articles for household, office or religious use.
Heading/subheading 63.09 refers only to the following goods: Items made of textile materials: Clothing and clothing accessories, and parts thereof.
Heading/subheading 67.01 does not apply to articles of clothing and clothing accessories in which feathers or down constitute no more than an ornament or padding;

This Chapter does not include: Sport bags or other containers in headings/subheadings 42.02, 43.03 or 43.04; [References: heading 42.02 – Trunks, suitcases, vanitycases, executivecases, briefcases, school satchels, spectacle cases, binocular cases, camera cases, musical instrument cases, gun cases, holsters and similar containers;...; heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; heading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

This Chapter does not include: Tableware, kitchenware, sanitary ware, carpets, other textile floor coverings, clothing accessories, bed linen, kitchen linen, toilet linen, similar products having a utilitarian function (classified according to the material of which they are made).

Garments which, ostensibly, are classifiable both in heading/subheading 62.10 and in other headings/subheadings in this Chapter, except for heading/subheading 62.09, shall be classified in heading/subheading 62.10. [References: heading 62.10 – Garments, made up of fabrics of heading 56.02, 56.03, 59.03, 59.06 or 59.07.; heading 62.09 – Babies garments and clothing accessories.]

This Chapter does not include: Clothing and clothing accessories of processed leather (except gloves, thumb gloves and mittens), with a lining of fur or artificial fur or to which fur or artificial fur are attached on the outside, except when attached solely for decoration (heading/subheading 43.03 or 43.04). [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; subheading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

Clothing and clothing accessories (except those exempted according to Rule 2) having a lining of furskin or of artificial fur, or to which furskin or artificial fur is attached on the outside, except where attached solely for ornamentation, are classified in heading/subheading 43.03 or 43.04, as the case may be. [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; heading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

Garments, which ostensibly can be classified both in heading/subheading 61.13 and in other headings/subheadings of this Chapter, except for heading/subheading 61.11, shall be classified in heading/subheading 61.13. [References: heading 61.13 – Garments, made up of knitted or crocheted fabrics of heading 59.03, 59.06 or 59.07.; heading 61.11 – Babies garments and clothing accessories, knitted or crocheted.]

Products in Chapters 56 to 63 containing two or more textile materials are to be regarded as consisting entirely of that textile material which would be selected for the classification of the product under Chapters 50 to 55 or heading/subheading 58.09, made of the same textile materials, pursuant to Rule 2 of this Part. For the application of this rule: In the case of textile products made of a base fabric and a hairy surface or a looped surface, the base fabric will not be taken into account. [

Textile clothing in various subheadings is classified in the subheadings relating to them, even if they are presented as sets for retail sale, unless the context otherwise requires. For the purposes of this rule, the expression "textile clothing" means clothing in subheadings 61.01 to 61.14 and subheadings 62.01 to 62.11. [References: subheading 61.01 – Mens or boys overcoats, carcoats, capes, cloaks, anoraks (including skijackets), windcheaters, windjackets and similar articles, knitted or croc

This Chapter does not include goods in heading/subheading 42.02 or 42.03 are subject to Rule 2(b) of Chapter 42; [References: heading 42.02 – Trunks, suitcases, vanitycases, executivecases, briefcases, school satchels, spectacle cases, binocular cases, camera cases, musical instrument cases, gun cases, holsters and similar containers;...; heading 42.03 – Articles of apparel and clothing accessories, of leather or of composition leather.; chapter 42 – Articles of leather; saddlery and harness; tr

This Chapter does not include items of heading/subheading 43.03 or 43.04; [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; heading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

Any reference in subheadings 06.03 or 06.04 to goods of any kind means also reference to bouquets of flowers, baskets of flowers, wreaths of flowers and similar articles, made wholly or partly of goods of that kind, without regard to other constituent materials. However, these subheadings do not include collages or similar decorative plaques in heading/subheading 97.01. [References: heading 97.01 – Paintings, drawings and pastels, executed entirely by hand, other than drawings of heading 49.06 a

Frames surrounding paintings, drawings, pastels, collages or similar decorative plaques, engravings, prints or lithographs are to be classified with these items, provided they are of a kind and value normally used with regard to these items. Frames that are not of a kind or value normally used with regard to the items mentioned in this general rule are to be classified separately.

Heading/subheading 49.01 also includes a collection of printed reproductions, such as works of art or paintings, with related text, contained in numbered pages suitable for binding in one or more volumes.

rules.rule_text: This Chapter does not include furniture which is a toy or lamps and lighting fittings which are toys (heading/subheading 95.03), billiard tables or other furniture specially constructed for games (heading/subheading 95.04), furniture for conjuring tricks or decorations (other than lighting chains), such as Chinese lanterns (heading/subheading 95.05). [References: heading 95.03 – Tricycles, scooters, pedal cars and similar wheeled toys; dolls carriages; dolls; other toys; reducedsize ("scale") mo

Heading/subheading 66.03 does not include parts, decorations or accessories of textile materials, or covers, sheaths, straps, umbrella sheaths and the like, of any material. Such goods, presented together, but not fitted to the articles of heading/subheading 66.01 or 66.02, are classified separately and are not considered as parts of those articles. [References: heading 66.01 – Umbrellas and sun umbrellas (including walkingstick umbrellas, garden umbrellas and similar umbrellas).; heading 66.02

Heading 39.25 refers only to architectural ornaments and decorations, such as flutings, cupolas, dovecotes; and also ornamental fountains, which are not products included in any preceding heading in Chapter Subheading II. [References: chapter 39 – Plastics and articles thereof]

In the entire Supplement, the expression 'parts for general use' means items in headings/subheadings 83.01, 83.02, 83.08, 83.10, and frames and mirrors of base metal, in heading/subheading 83.06. [References: heading 83.01 – Padlocks and locks (key, combination or electrically operated), of base metal; clasps and frames with clasps, incorporating locks, of base metal; keys for any of the foregoing articles, of base metal.; heading 83.02 – Base metal mountings, fittings and similar articles suita

For the purposes of heading/subheading 64.06, the term "parts" does not include nails (pegs), buckles, eyelet rings, hooks, fasteners, ornaments, braids, laces, pompons or other trimmings (to be classified in the appropriate headings/subheadings) or buttons or other goods of heading/subheading 96.06. [References: heading 96.06 – Buttons, pressfasteners, snapfasteners and pressstuds, button moulds and other parts of these articles; button blanks.]

The expressions 'parts' and 'parts and accessories' do not refer to items in heading/subheading 83.06, if they can be identified as being for goods in this part or not. [References: heading 83.06 – Bells, gongs and the like, nonelectric, of base metal; statuettes and other ornaments, of base metal; photograph, picture or similar frames, of base metal; mirrors of base metal.]

Headings/Subheadings 44.14 to 44.21 refer to the items described therein, made of particle board or similar board, fiberboard, laminated wood or densified wood, as they refer to such items made of wood. [References: heading 44.14 – Wooden frames for paintings, photographs, mirrors or similar objects.; heading 44.15 – Packing cases, boxes, crates, drums and similar packings, of wood; cabledrums of wood; pallets, box pallets and other load boards, of wood; pallet collars of wood.; heading 44.16 –

For the purposes of heading/subheading 71.14, the expression "articles of goldsmiths' or silversmiths' wares" includes items such as ornaments, tableware, toilet articles, smoking accessories, and other articles for household, office or religious use.
Heading/subheading 63.09 refers only to the following goods: Items made of textile materials: Clothing and clothing accessories, and parts thereof.
Heading/subheading 67.01 does not apply to articles of clothing and clothing accessories in which feathers or down constitute no more than an ornament or padding;

This Chapter does not include: Sport bags or other containers in headings/subheadings 42.02, 43.03 or 43.04; [References: heading 42.02 – Trunks, suitcases, vanitycases, executivecases, briefcases, school satchels, spectacle cases, binocular cases, camera cases, musical instrument cases, gun cases, holsters and similar containers;...; heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; heading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

This Chapter does not include: Tableware, kitchenware, sanitary ware, carpets, other textile floor coverings, clothing accessories, bed linen, kitchen linen, toilet linen, similar products having a utilitarian function (classified according to the material of which they are made).

Garments which, ostensibly, are classifiable both in heading/subheading 62.10 and in other headings/subheadings in this Chapter, except for heading/subheading 62.09, shall be classified in heading/subheading 62.10. [References: heading 62.10 – Garments, made up of fabrics of heading 56.02, 56.03, 59.03, 59.06 or 59.07.; heading 62.09 – Babies garments and clothing accessories.]

This Chapter does not include: Clothing and clothing accessories of processed leather (except gloves, thumb gloves and mittens), with a lining of fur or artificial fur or to which fur or artificial fur are attached on the outside, except when attached solely for decoration (heading/subheading 43.03 or 43.04). [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; subheading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

Clothing and clothing accessories (except those exempted according to Rule 2) having a lining of furskin or of artificial fur, or to which furskin or artificial fur is attached on the outside, except where attached solely for ornamentation, are classified in heading/subheading 43.03 or 43.04, as the case may be. [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; heading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

Garments, which ostensibly can be classified both in heading/subheading 61.13 and in other headings/subheadings of this Chapter, except for heading/subheading 61.11, shall be classified in heading/subheading 61.13. [References: heading 61.13 – Garments, made up of knitted or crocheted fabrics of heading 59.03, 59.06 or 59.07.; heading 61.11 – Babies garments and clothing accessories, knitted or crocheted.]

Products in Chapters 56 to 63 containing two or more textile materials are to be regarded as consisting entirely of that textile material which would be selected for the classification of the product under Chapters 50 to 55 or heading/subheading 58.09, made of the same textile materials, pursuant to Rule 2 of this Part. For the application of this rule: In the case of textile products made of a base fabric and a hairy surface or a looped surface, the base fabric will not be taken into account. [

Textile clothing in various subheadings is classified in the subheadings relating to them, even if they are presented as sets for retail sale, unless the context otherwise requires. For the purposes of this rule, the expression "textile clothing" means clothing in subheadings 61.01 to 61.14 and subheadings 62.01 to 62.11. [References: subheading 61.01 – Mens or boys overcoats, carcoats, capes, cloaks, anoraks (including skijackets), windcheaters, windjackets and similar articles, knitted or croc

This Chapter does not include goods in heading/subheading 42.02 or 42.03 are subject to Rule 2(b) of Chapter 42; [References: heading 42.02 – Trunks, suitcases, vanitycases, executivecases, briefcases, school satchels, spectacle cases, binocular cases, camera cases, musical instrument cases, gun cases, holsters and similar containers;...; heading 42.03 – Articles of apparel and clothing accessories, of leather or of composition leather.; chapter 42 – Articles of leather; saddlery and harness; tr

This Chapter does not include items of heading/subheading 43.03 or 43.04; [References: heading 43.03 – Articles of apparel, clothing accessories and other articles of furskin.; heading 43.04 – Artificial fur and articles thereof.]

Any reference in subheadings 06.03 or 06.04 to goods of any kind means also reference to bouquets of flowers, baskets of flowers, wreaths of flowers and similar articles, made wholly or partly of goods of that kind, without regard to other constituent materials. However, these subheadings do not include collages or similar decorative plaques in heading/subheading 97.01. [References: heading 97.01 – Paintings, drawings and pastels, executed entirely by hand, other than drawings of heading 49.06 a

Frames surrounding paintings, drawings, pastels, collages or similar decorative plaques, engravings, prints or lithographs are to be classified with these items, provided they are of a kind and value normally used with regard to these items. Frames that are not of a kind or value normally used with regard to the items mentioned in this general rule are to be classified separately.

Heading/subheading 49.01 also includes a collection of printed reproductions, such as works of art or paintings, with related text, contained in numbered pages suitable for binding in one or more volumes.

Normal operations can be actuated via the PL640 toggle switch. Toggle switch position Function 1 (lever left) Normal operations 2 (lever right) Inspection travel 2.2 Inspection travel ! Warning! Danger from the inspection travel being made use of ! Use of inspection travel may result in serious accidents which, in turn, may lead to serious or fatal injuries. Therefore: 12 • Make sure before any inspection travel that nobody is in the danger zone. ! Warning! Inappropriately handling the inspection travel can lead to substantial personal injuries and material damage. Therefore: • Only service personnel are allowed to operate the inspection travel. Given maintenance and fitting work to be undertaken under inspection travel, the lift can be moved inch by inch. The inspection travel operating elements are on the PL640 control printed circuit board. The printed circuit board cover must be removed to operate the inspection travel. Inspection travel can be actuated via the PL640 toggle switch. Toggle switch position 1 (lever left) 2 (lever right) Function Normal operation Inspection travel With inspection travel turned on, no further travel commands are taken on. The car can only be moved by pressing the up and down keys. Inspection travel can only be activated when the safety circuit is closed. As such, it cannot be used for retrieval, for instance, from the emergency limit switch. The in-use lamps flash at the landing doors when inspection travel is ongoing. BKG ! Caution! Operating modes Moving the car as part of inspection travel means there is no automatic lift stopping at the end stops. The lift either travels up to the emergency limit switches or lands on the mechanical stoppers. On completion of the maintenance work, the PL640 printed circuit board toggle switch must be made use of to turn off the inspection travel. The printed circuit board cover is put back on and from a push-button panel a travel command is sent to either the top or bottom floor. 13 Functions 3 Functions 3.1 Visual display 3.1.1 Location indicator The location indicator tells the user where the lift currently is. BKG 3.1.2 Call acknowledgement 3.1.3 In-use indicator To show the user that the travel command has been accepted, the illuminated display of the button pressed flashes. The illuminated display of the selected floor flashes in the push-button panels of every floor until the lift has reached its destination floor. The in-use indicator lights up when A door is still open The lift travels off. 3.2 Button 3.2.1 Call button 3.2.2 Send button The in-use indicator flashes when A malfunction has arisen The installation run is switched on No travel commands are taken on by the controller for as long as the in-use indicator either lights up or flashes. Pressing the call button brings the lift to one's floor. The call button is green. Pressing the send button sends the lift to a different floor. The send buttons are white. 3.2.3 Signalling button A signal sounds when the lift with open door is at a floor and the red button is pressed. 3.3.1 3.3 Acoustic signals Arrival signal An acoustic signal sounds for the time set on the lift having reached the stop. 3.3.2 Buzzer 14 A signal sounds when the lift with open door is at a floor and the red button is pressed. The point of this acoustic signal is for communication purposes between the floors in that the user is asked to close the door. BKG Functions 3.4 Lamp test The lamp test is used to test the functionality of the illuminated signallers and buttons in the push-button panels. The lamp test is activated when the installation run is switched on. When a button is pressed, the corresponding illuminated signaller lights up. On the in-use indicator and current location indicator, the illuminated signaller goes out when the button is pressed. If the illuminated signaller does not react to the button, then this indicates a defective lamp or button (or a wiring fault). 3.5 Test run Travel commands can be given using the operating elements on the control printed circuit board. BKG 4 Connection and Setting 4.1 Control panel 4.1.1 Assembly in the machine room 4 Warning - Risk from electrical current! Connection and Setting Some of the control system and electrical component voltages are potentially lethal. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: • • Mains switch and/or building-side fuses are to be isolated before the control panel is removed from the guiding section. Only when the control panel has been mounted in the guiding section is the voltage to be turned on again. To make it easier to get at the equipment in the machine room, the control panel can be moved on the guiding section or taken from it and mounted on the machine room door. Once the maintenance work is over, the control panel is to be put back into the guiding section. 4.1.2 Controller in the control cabinet The controller can also be fitted into a control cabinet which is optionally available. An additional mains switch must be installed in the machine room if the control panel cannot be seen from it. 4.2 Installation of the shaft wiring The floor junction boxes are to be fitted at the floors in keeping with the lift drawing. A floor junction box is part of each floor. The boxes are equipped at the floors in keeping with the actual appliances and are marked from X1 to X27. Box X1 is at the lowest floor and Box X27 at the uppermost. Boxes X2 – X5 - if present - are assigned to the middle floors. The floor junction box contains the PL625 safety circuit printed circuit board and the PL621 control printed circuit board. The floor junction boxes are connected by the control and safety cables. To this end, the cables are installed through the corner rod of the shaft structure and secured with clamps. The circuit and wiring drawings form the basis for the electrical installation of the floor junction boxes and equipment on the floors. The equipment cables at the floors are directed into the floor junction boxes and linked via connectors with the appropriate PL621 / PL625 printed circuit boards. The equipment connecting cables are installed at the shaft structure belts and secured with cable bands. To relieve tension, the cables are to be fixed with cable bands at the floor junction boxes. The cable bands are to be pulled through the ports at the side of the floor junction boxes and the cables fixed to them. 17 BKG Connection and Setting ! Caution - Damage to cables! The cables are to be installed well away from the car, counterweight, door locks and other moving components. During installation the bending radii are to be adhered to. Any pronounced kinks in the cables are to be avoided. Bending radius = 4 x cable diameter. 4.3 Floor switch 4.3.1 Lifts with 2 stops Pointer The lift drawing specifies where the floor junction box is located. All cable lengths have been calculated for this arrangement. Any other arrangement of the shaft installation might result in the calculated cable lengths being no longer adequate. The car position is recorded by the floor switches. A floor switch is assigned to each floor. Bi-stable solenoid-operated switches are used. The solenoid-operated switches are proximity-connected via 2 actuating magnets. Switching is done as a function of poling and direction. It is vital that the following points are followed when undertaking installation: • • • • The solenoid-operated magnet is to be fitted so that the connecting cable hangs down. Note the positions of the actuating magnets! Red magnet at the top, green magnet below. Actuating magnet and solenoid-operating switch are not to be over 10mm apart. With the lift stopped, the solenoid-operating switch is located between the red and green actuating magnets. The solenoid-operated switches are set at 50%b capacity. Select the actuating magnet spacing so that the solenoid-operated switch is between the red and green actuating magnet once the lift stops. The solenoid-operated switches are now to be moved on the holding devices so that the lift stops flush with the floors. 4.3.2 Lifts with 3 to 6 stops 18 The solenoid-operated switches are set at 50%b capacity. Adjustment work is begun at one of the middle floors. Select the actuating magnet spacing so that the lift stops between the red and green actuating magnets. The spacing of the actuating magnets is now reduced to the extent that the lift stops at the same position whether going down or going up. In going down, the lift stops when the green actuating magnet is reached. In going up, the lift stops when the red actuating magnet is reached. Only now are the solenoid-operated switches at the floors to be moved on the holding devices to the extent that the lift stops flush with them. BKG Connection and Setting Pointer To improve the arriving precision of <= 0.1 m/s lifts, two solenoid-operated switches are connected in parallel in the middle floors. The solenoid-operated switches are operated via 2 separate magnetic tracks. 4.4 Mounting the trailing cable ! The trailing cable contacts the car electrical equipment with the controller. There is a mounting bracket under the car for fastening the trailing cable. The trailing cable is directed into the car junction box and secured with cable bands. Halfway up the shaft, the trailing cable with its holder is fastened to a shaft structure belt and then run all the way to the controller. The trailing cable is electrically installed on the basis of the circuit and wiring plans. Caution - Damage to the trailing cable! The trailing cable must be twist-free and hang well away from the structure in the shaft. With the car in the end positions, the trailing cable is to hang freely. It must not be under tension or lie on the bottom of the shaft pit. The bending radius of the trailing cable is to be adhered to. Bending radius 10 x line thickness Flat cable Round cable 20 x cable diameter 19 BKG Connection and Setting 4.5 Safety and locking circuit ! 4.5.1 In the shaft All safety switches, including door contacts, emergency limit switches, emergency braking switches, load-bearing element control switches, form part of the safety circuit. All safety switches are connected in series. The safety circuit contacts are, on no account, to be parallel-connected or bridged. Warning! Risk of injury from bridging the safety circuit! Bridging the safety circuit or individual safety switches can lead to serious injuries and even to fatal ones. Therefore: Never bridge the safety circuit or individual safety switches! The locking circuit is arranged downstream of the safety circuit and controls door locking. (only applies to lifts with magnetic locking cams.) Various safety switches may be used depending on the lift type. The lift safety switches can be seen from the circuit diagrams. A PL625 safety circuit printed circuit board can be found in every floor junction box. Plugs connect the safety switches to the printed circuit board. Plug-in connections are to correspond to the specifications of the circuit and wiring plans. Flat connectors are used for connecting up the PE conductor. Assignment of the plug-in connections: 3-pin grey 2-pin grey Riser line Plug-in connection Safety switch 2-pin black Plug-in connection Locking switch Flat connector PE conductor connection 4.5.2 At the car 20 Terminal blocks are used to connect up the safety switches at the car in the car junction box. The car safety switches are brought together in the car junction box and connected to the controller via the suspended cable. Connection is by means of terminal blocks which are to correspond to the specifications of the circuit and wiring plans. BKG Connection and Setting 4.5.3 Checking the safety switches ! 4 Warning! Risk of injury from faulty safety and locking circuits! A faulty safety circuit can lead to serious injuries which may be fatal. Therefore: Check on every safety and locking switch as to working order. Warning - Risk from electrical current! Risk to life from electrical current! There is a direct risk to life from coming into contact with energized parts. Therefore: Only have work on the electrical system carried out by electrical skilled workers. • Do not bridge the safety switches. • • Electrical safety equipment tests must be carried out to comply with EN81- 3 Annex D. Examine each safety switch on the basis of the circuit diagram and a suitable measuring instrument. 4.6 Drive unit connection A Warning - Risk from electrical current! Potentially lethal voltages are present at the drive unit. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: 4.6.1 Direction of rotation • Isolate mains switch before any work on the drive unit. • • Secure against the mains switch being turned on again. Check on isolation from power supply. In case of a wrong direction of rotation, the U and V leads of the motor cable must be swapped round. 4.6.2 Motor protection switch The motor protection switch is to be adjusted to the motor rated current. Motor rated current details can be obtained from the motor type plate. 21 Connection and Setting BKG 4.7 Mains connection ! Warning - Risk from electrical current! Some of the control system and electrical component voltage is potentially lethal. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: • • • Isolate mains switch and fuses on the building side prior to connecting the controller to the mains network. Check on isolation from power supply. Secure against the mains switch being turned on again. Before connecting the controller to the mains network it must be ensured that • • • All electrical components and modules are effectively connected to the protective circuit. All metallic components - in particular the shaft structure - are effectively connected to the equipotential bonding provided by others. All safety switches are connected and in working order. Caution - Damage to components! Check on the following before connection to the supply network: • • Does the mains voltage conform with the lift specifications? It is absolutely necessary that the specification requirements of the lift for the building-side fusing are adhered to! Connect the supply mains lead with the controller in accordance with the circuit diagram. The leads to the control panel are to be arch-like installed and must be long enough for the control panel to be moved on the guide section or hung at the machine room door. 22 Pointer The connection line as provided by others to the control panel must be suitable for flexible cable routing purposes. To relieve tension, the leads are to be fixed with cable bands at the control panel. The cable bands are to be pulled through the ports underneath the control panel sheet metal and the leads fixed to them. Three-phase controllers are fitted out with a phase control relay. Given a correct phase sequence, the relay contact switches/closes and the appropriate LED lights up. The fact of the LED not lighting up points to either the lack of a phase or the need for the input rotating field at the L1, L2 and L3 terminals to be replaced. BKG Connection and Setting 4.8 Pre-commissioning examination 4.8.1 Measuring the current Use a suitable instrument (pliers-type ammeter) to measure the current input at the L1/L2/L3 terminals during operations and verify it on the basis of the lift's nominal data. 4.8.2 Testing the electrical cables Warning - Risk from electrical current! Some of the control system and electrical component voltages are potentially lethal. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: 4.8.2.1 • Turn off the mains switch before testing the cables. • Check on isolation from power supply. • Secure against the mains switch being turned on again. Measuring the insulation resistance ! Caution - Damage to components! To protect the electronic system, the L1/L2/L3 outer conductors must be connected with the N neutral conductor. An appropriate insulation instrument is to be used to measure the insulation resistance. Measuring is undertaken on the terminals of every electrical appliance the supply voltage of which is in excess of 50 V. 4.8.2.2 Examination the PE conductor An appropriate instrument is to be used to check on the connection of the PE conductor to those parts of the lift which may be unintentionally energized. 4.8.3 Checking the safety switches • Do not bridge the safety switches. The electrical safety equipment is to be tested in keeping with EN60204-31. On the basis of the circuit and wiring plans, a suitable instrument is to be used to check on every safety switch. 23 BKG Connection and Setting 4.8.4 Travel time control testing 4 Warning - Risk from electrical current! With the controller turned off, none of the illuminated displays light up and no travel commands are accepted by the controller. Even following a controller shutdown by means of the key-operated switch or button, the lift can still be released for a limited number of users or secured against unauthorized use. Pointer The lift should be shut down at the mains switch in the case of lengthy breaks between use. ! Warning! Making use of the key-operated switch/button to shut down the controller is not suitable for an assured immobilization of the lift for maintenance purposes. Maintenance work carried out in the danger zone when the lift has not been immobilized can result in serious injuries and may be lethal. Therefore: Turn off the mains switch and prevent it being turned on again for an assured immobilization of the lift. 4 Warning! Even with the controller turned off via the key-operated switch/button, sections of the control system continue to be under extremely dangerous voltage. Touching live parts can lead to very serious injuries and may be lethal! Therefore: • Turn off the mains switch and prevent it being turned on again before working on the controller. Check on isolation from power supply. In instances where the lift has a key-operated switch, the controller can only be turned on and off from one floor. Key-operated buttons need to be deployed should it be possible to turn the lift on and off at a number of floors. The function required "Button" or "Switch" must be activated at the PL640 Control Printed Circuit Board. For the purpose of classifying goods in this Chapter, the weight shall be considered as the weight of a motor vehicle in a condition fit for operation.

A motor vehicle will be classified in subheading 87.03.2150 and in subheading 87.03.9050 if it has four wheels which are connected directly, without suspension, to a front axle with steering and to a rear axle driven by an engine; the diameter of its wheel rim does not exceed 6 inches; its length does not exceed 205 cm; and the height from the floor (without the seat and without the headrest) does not exceed 65 cm.
Heading/subheading 86.07 refers, inter alia, to rail vehicles.

2. *Principally designed for transport of persons*: The Panamera is a four‑door luxury sedan whose chief function is to carry passengers; this is inherent to the vehicle type, thus definitively met.  
3. *Must not be those of heading 87.02*: Heading 87.02 applies to buses (≥10 seats). The Panamera seats at most five, so it is certainly outside that heading – definitively met.

[References: chapter XVII – Section XVII: VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT]
Rules for Section XVI: This Section does not include: Items in Part XVII; [References: section XVII – Section XVII: VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT]
For the purpose of classifying goods in this Chapter, the weight shall be considered as the weight of a motor vehicle in a condition fit for operation.

A motor vehicle will be classified in subheading 87.03.2150 and in subheading 87.03.9050 if it has four wheels which are connected directly, without suspension, to a front axle with steering and to a rear axle driven by an engine; the diameter of its wheel rim does not exceed 6 inches; its length does not exceed 205 cm; and the height from the floor (without the seat and without the headrest) does not exceed 65 cm.
Heading/subheading 86.07 refers, inter alia, to rail vehicles.
